description:
A carrier's roadside inspection, violation and crash summary on its
own. Paid, flat price; billed whenever the USDOT number resolves, even if
the carrier had no inspections (that is the finding). An unknown number is
a free not_found.

inspections (SMS data, a 24-month window that ends weeks before today:
read window_end): inspection counts by driver and vehicle, out-of-service
counts and rates (FMCSA's own method; no national average is carried, so
cite FMCSA's), violation counts in total and by BASIC, last inspection
date. When there were no inspections the measures are null, never zero,
and data_quality_flags says why: inspection_summary_no_inspections (in
SMS, none in the window) or inspection_summary_unavailable (in neither
SMS file, so SMS says nothing either way). A carrier inspected only after
window_end reads as having none.

crashes (federally recordable crashes, trailing 730 days ending at the
build date): counts by fatal, injury, tow-away and hazmat release, plus
fatalities and injuries and the last crash date. A floor, not a total:
about 19% of crash records carry no USDOT number and cannot be attributed
to any carrier.

Counts, not a rating: this does not say a carrier is safe or unsafe, and
it carries no contact information.
